items.title: What Is T3 Code? Key Features, Setup & Limitations Guide
items.summary: As AI coding tools continue to evolve, tools like Claude Code and Codex can independently handle code writing, debugging, and testing. However, working with multiple tools also introduces challenges, including frequent switching, complex task management, and code conflicts, while increasing operational overhead. T3 Code is an open-source AI Agent management tool that brings multiple coding agents together in one interface. It supports parallel tasks and isolated coding environments. This guide explains its core features, installation and configuration steps, and key limitations. I. What Is T3 Code? How Is It Different from AI Coding Tools? T3 Code is an open-source AI coding agent management tool developed by the T3 Tools team. It is designed as an Agent Harness Control Surface. Rather than being an AI model or standalone coding agent, it serves as a unified interface for accessing AI coding tools and their existing authentication configurations on a developer’s local machine. Unlike Claude Code and Codex, which focus on code generation and task execution, T3 Code focuses on integrating multiple coding agents. Developers can use different tools within the same interface. For example, they can assign one development task to Codex and switch to Claude Code for another without moving between separate applications. In terms of its overall positioning, T3 Code focuses on multi-tool integration, centralized task management, and flexible collaboration. It is particularly suitable for developers who need to work with multiple AI coding tools simultaneously. II. What Problems Does T3 Code Solve? Key Development Use Cases 1. Switching Between Multiple AI Coding Tools Is Time-Consuming Different coding agents have their own strengths in code generation, debugging, and problem analysis. Using them separately requires developers to switch between tools repeatedly. With T3 Code, developers can access different agents from a unified interface, compare their implementations of the same requirement, and select the most suitable solution. Use case: Developers who have high code quality requirements and need to compare the performance of tools like Claude Code and Codex, or flexibly select agents based on different task types. 2. Parallel Development Tasks Can Cause Code Conflicts When multiple tasks run in parallel, file overwrites and code modification conflicts can occur. T3 Code supports Git Worktrees, allowing each Thread to have its own independent working directory so that tasks can run on separate branches. After a task is completed, developers can review code differences, manage commits, and create Pull Requests. Use case: Developers working on multiple features simultaneously, fixing different bugs, or assigning multiple agents to handle tasks within the same project in parallel. 3. Complex Development Tasks Require Collaborative Workflows AI agents may need to modify files and execute commands when performing tasks. Excessive permissions can increase the risk of unintended operations. T3 Code provides different permission modes, including supervised, auto-accept edits, auto, and full access. Developers can adjust the scope of agent permissions according to task complexity and risk. Use case: Developers who need to run automated coding tasks while controlling file modification and command execution permissions. This is particularly useful for important projects or workflows that require manual review. 4. Developers Need to Monitor Progress Remotely Long-running coding tasks require continuous monitoring, but developers do not need to remain in front of a terminal at all times. T3 Code supports remote access through web, desktop, and mobile interfaces, allowing developers to check agent status and output and interact with agents when necessary. Use case: Developers who need to run long-running coding tasks or remotely monitor development progress. However, the actual coding process still runs on the host machine where the agent is running. This device must remain powered on and accessible. III. T3 Code Tutorial: Environment Preparation, Installation, and Configuration Step 1: Install and Launch T3 Code T3 Code supports command-line installation and also provides a desktop application. This guide uses the command-line installation method. For macOS and Linux users, open a terminal and run the official installation command: curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh Windows users can execute the following command in PowerShell: irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex After installation, you can start the T3 Code service and open the local web console. If you do not want to install it yet, you can also try it using npx t3@latest. However, Node.js and npm must be installed beforehand. If the system reports that the t3 command cannot be found, check whether the installation directory has been added to the system PATH. Step 2: Configure Providers and Connect AI Coding Agents After entering the console, go to Settings → Providers and select the AI coding agents you want to use. Note that T3 Code does not provide its own model usage credits. You must install the corresponding Provider CLI and complete account login or API authentication beforehand. The built-in and compatible Providers currently supported by the project include: Codex Claude Code Cursor OpenCode … Some tools require CLI installation and account authorization in advance. For example, Claude Code supports the following authentication command: claude auth login Other supported authentication methods may also be available depending on the version and environment. Finally, make sure at least one available Provider is configured before creating and running coding tasks. Step 3: Connect Your Local Development Environment and Project Next, connect T3 Code to your local development project. Open the project management interface, select the environment where the agent will run, and then add or open your local project directory. Make sure the project path is correct, the Git repository is in a normal state, and the current environment has permission to read and modify project files. If you use a remote server or WSL as the runtime environment, install the required Provider CLI and complete authentication within that environment beforehand. This ensures that the agent can access the project properly. Step 4: Configure Models, Task Assignments, and Network Settings After creating a Thread, select the Provider and available model according to your development requirements, then configure the permission mode. For first-time users, supervised mode is recommended. Once you become familiar with the agent’s workflow, you can gradually adjust its automation permissions. During task execution, the underlying AI agent needs to continuously send requests to model services and receive responses for code generation, analysis, and debugging. Restricted network access, unstable connections, or frequent changes to network exits may cause request timeouts and connection interruptions, affecting task execution. If these issues occur, first check your network connection, DNS settings, and Provider service status. If you need to change the network exit, you can configure a proxy IP for the underlying agent. For agents that support HTTP proxy environment variables, you can set them in the startup environment as follows: export HTTPS_PROXY="http://username:password@IP:PORT" export HTTP_PROXY="http://username:password@IP:PORT" For these scenarios, choose a proxy provider that supports the proxy protocols required by your agent, such as IPFoxy . Obtain the corresponding proxy connection details and enter the username, password, IP address, and port in the specified format. After configuring the environment variables and restarting the agent, the proxy IP will be enabled in the current runtime environment, allowing the agent to access model services through the designated network exit. For development tasks that need to run over extended periods, you can also consider using IPFoxy residential proxies. They provide relatively stable network exits through real residential broadband IP addresses, helping agents maintain connections to model services and reduce connection issues caused by frequent changes in network exits. Step 5: Run Your First Task and Review the Results After completing the configuration, create a Thread for testing. It is recommended to start with a simple, clearly defined task, such as fixing a bug, adjusting a page style, or adding test code. After launching the task, observe whether the agent can read project files, execute operations, and return results normally. Once the task is complete, open the code Diff to review the specific changes and run the project tests. After confirming that the functionality meets expectations, commit the code or merge it into the main branch. Avoid allowing unreviewed modifications to enter the production project directly. IV. T3 Code Limitations and Important Considerations 1. Multi-Agent Orchestration and Environment Configuration T3 Code allows multiple agents to collaborate on complex development tasks. One approach is to have a parent agent analyze requirements, break them down into subtasks, and define the execution order. Different child agents can then handle code writing, bug investigation, and code reviews. Finally, the parent agent consolidates the results, checks task completion, and coordinates any follow-up modifications. However, if multiple agents share account credentials, environment variables, or proxy configurations, authentication information may be overwritten or proxy exits may be mixed up. This can cause agents to use the wrong accounts, experience connection issues, or even interrupt tasks. Therefore, it is recommended to store proxy information and other configuration details for different agents in separate scripts. This makes them easier to manage and call while reducing interference between runtime environments. 2. Dependence on Third-Party AI Coding Agents T3 Code does not provide its own AI models. Code generation quality, response speed, and usage limits depend on the underlying Providers. Before using it, make sure the corresponding tools have completed authentication, your account subscription or API credits are sufficient, and the CLI version is compatible with the current version of T3 Code. If an agent fails to execute a request, check the Provider’s service status and authentication information first. 3. Automated Permissions Do Not Mean Zero Operational Risk T3 Code provides different permission modes, but granting higher permissions allows agents to perform operations such as modifying files and executing terminal commands. For high-risk tasks involving file deletion, configuration changes, or system commands, it is recommended to retain manual approval and review commands and modification scopes before execution. V. Additional compatible agents can also be integrated through methods such as ACP. The actual supported tools depend on the current version. Q2: Can T3 Code Run Multiple AI Agents Simultaneously? Yes. Users can create multiple Threads to let different agents handle tasks in parallel. Git Worktrees can also be used to isolate coding environments. The actual number of parallel tasks depends on available device resources and Provider usage limits. Q3: Does T3 Code Need to Run on a Computer All the Time? If agents run in a local environment, the computer or server must remain powered on. Remote access only allows you to switch devices for managing tasks; it does not automatically move the tasks to the cloud. VI. Conclusion The main value of T3 Code lies in its ability to centrally manage multiple AI coding agents, simplify task assignment, and support parallel development. It is suitable for developers who need to switch between agents, manage multiple projects, and monitor tasks remotely. However, its actual capabilities are still subject to third-party services and runtime environments. Before using it, make sure your accounts, permissions, and environment configurations are properly set up. What Is T3 Code? items.summary_html:
As AI coding tools continue to evolve, tools like Claude Code and Codex can independently handle code writing, debugging, and testing. However, working with multiple tools also introduces challenges, including frequent switching, complex task management, and code conflicts, while increasing operational overhead.

T3 Code is an open-source AI Agent management tool that brings multiple coding agents together in one interface. It supports parallel tasks and isolated coding environments. This guide explains its core features, installation and configuration steps, and key limitations.

I. What Is T3 Code? How Is It Different from AI Coding Tools?

T3 Code is an open-source AI coding agent management tool developed by the T3 Tools team. It is designed as an Agent Harness Control Surface. Rather than being an AI model or standalone coding agent, it serves as a unified interface for accessing AI coding tools and their existing authentication configurations on a developer’s local machine.

Unlike Claude Code and Codex, which focus on code generation and task execution, T3 Code focuses on integrating multiple coding agents. Developers can use different tools within the same interface. For example, they can assign one development task to Codex and switch to Claude Code for another without moving between separate applications.

In terms of its overall positioning, T3 Code focuses on multi-tool integration, centralized task management, and flexible collaboration. It is particularly suitable for developers who need to work with multiple AI coding tools simultaneously.

II. What Problems Does T3 Code Solve? Key Development Use Cases1. Switching Between Multiple AI Coding Tools Is Time-Consuming

Different coding agents have their own strengths in code generation, debugging, and problem analysis. Using them separately requires developers to switch between tools repeatedly. With T3 Code, developers can access different agents from a unified interface, compare their implementations of the same requirement, and select the most suitable solution.

Use case: Developers who have high code quality requirements and need to compare the performance of tools like Claude Code and Codex, or flexibly select agents based on different task types.

2. Parallel Development Tasks Can Cause Code Conflicts

When multiple tasks run in parallel, file overwrites and code modification conflicts can occur. T3 Code supports Git Worktrees, allowing each Thread to have its own independent working directory so that tasks can run on separate branches.

After a task is completed, developers can review code differences, manage commits, and create Pull Requests.

Use case: Developers working on multiple features simultaneously, fixing different bugs, or assigning multiple agents to handle tasks within the same project in parallel.

3. Complex Development Tasks Require Collaborative Workflows

AI agents may need to modify files and execute commands when performing tasks. Excessive permissions can increase the risk of unintended operations.

T3 Code provides different permission modes, including supervised, auto-accept edits, auto, and full access. Developers can adjust the scope of agent permissions according to task complexity and risk.

Use case: Developers who need to run automated coding tasks while controlling file modification and command execution permissions. This is particularly useful for important projects or workflows that require manual review.

4. Developers Need to Monitor Progress Remotely

Long-running coding tasks require continuous monitoring, but developers do not need to remain in front of a terminal at all times. T3 Code supports remote access through web, desktop, and mobile interfaces, allowing developers to check agent status and output and interact with agents when necessary.

Use case: Developers who need to run long-running coding tasks or remotely monitor development progress. However, the actual coding process still runs on the host machine where the agent is running. This device must remain powered on and accessible.

III. T3 Code Tutorial: Environment Preparation, Installation, and ConfigurationStep 1: Install and Launch T3 Code

T3 Code supports command-line installation and also provides a desktop application. This guide uses the command-line installation method.

For macOS and Linux users, open a terminal and run the official installation command:

curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh

Windows users can execute the following command in PowerShell:

irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex

After installation, you can start the T3 Code service and open the local web console.

If you do not want to install it yet, you can also try it using npx t3@latest. However, Node.js and npm must be installed beforehand.

If the system reports that the t3 command cannot be found, check whether the installation directory has been added to the system PATH.

Step 2: Configure Providers and Connect AI Coding Agents

After entering the console, go to Settings → Providers and select the AI coding agents you want to use.

Note that T3 Code does not provide its own model usage credits. You must install the corresponding Provider CLI and complete account login or API authentication beforehand.

The built-in and compatible Providers currently supported by the project include:

  1. Codex
  2. Claude Code
  3. Cursor
  4. OpenCode
  5. …

Some tools require CLI installation and account authorization in advance. For example, Claude Code supports the following authentication command:

claude auth login

Other supported authentication methods may also be available depending on the version and environment.

Finally, make sure at least one available Provider is configured before creating and running coding tasks.

Step 3: Connect Your Local Development Environment and Project

Next, connect T3 Code to your local development project. Open the project management interface, select the environment where the agent will run, and then add or open your local project directory.

Make sure the project path is correct, the Git repository is in a normal state, and the current environment has permission to read and modify project files.

If you use a remote server or WSL as the runtime environment, install the required Provider CLI and complete authentication within that environment beforehand. This ensures that the agent can access the project properly.

Step 4: Configure Models, Task Assignments, and Network Settings

After creating a Thread, select the Provider and available model according to your development requirements, then configure the permission mode.

For first-time users, supervised mode is recommended. Once you become familiar with the agent’s workflow, you can gradually adjust its automation permissions.

During task execution, the underlying AI agent needs to continuously send requests to model services and receive responses for code generation, analysis, and debugging. Restricted network access, unstable connections, or frequent changes to network exits may cause request timeouts and connection interruptions, affecting task execution.

If these issues occur, first check your network connection, DNS settings, and Provider service status.

If you need to change the network exit, you can configure a proxy IP for the underlying agent. For agents that support HTTP proxy environment variables, you can set them in the startup environment as follows:

export HTTPS_PROXY="http://username:password@IP:PORT"
export HTTP_PROXY="http://username:password@IP:PORT"

For these scenarios, choose a proxy provider that supports the proxy protocols required by your agent, such as IPFoxy. Obtain the corresponding proxy connection details and enter the username, password, IP address, and port in the specified format.

After configuring the environment variables and restarting the agent, the proxy IP will be enabled in the current runtime environment, allowing the agent to access model services through the designated network exit.

For development tasks that need to run over extended periods, you can also consider using IPFoxy residential proxies. They provide relatively stable network exits through real residential broadband IP addresses, helping agents maintain connections to model services and reduce connection issues caused by frequent changes in network exits.

Step 5: Run Your First Task and Review the Results

After completing the configuration, create a Thread for testing.

It is recommended to start with a simple, clearly defined task, such as fixing a bug, adjusting a page style, or adding test code. After launching the task, observe whether the agent can read project files, execute operations, and return results normally.

Once the task is complete, open the code Diff to review the specific changes and run the project tests.

After confirming that the functionality meets expectations, commit the code or merge it into the main branch. Avoid allowing unreviewed modifications to enter the production project directly.

IV. T3 Code Limitations and Important Considerations1. Multi-Agent Orchestration and Environment Configuration

T3 Code allows multiple agents to collaborate on complex development tasks. One approach is to have a parent agent analyze requirements, break them down into subtasks, and define the execution order. Different child agents can then handle code writing, bug investigation, and code reviews. Finally, the parent agent consolidates the results, checks task completion, and coordinates any follow-up modifications.

However, if multiple agents share account credentials, environment variables, or proxy configurations, authentication information may be overwritten or proxy exits may be mixed up. This can cause agents to use the wrong accounts, experience connection issues, or even interrupt tasks.

Therefore, it is recommended to store proxy information and other configuration details for different agents in separate scripts. This makes them easier to manage and call while reducing interference between runtime environments.

2. Dependence on Third-Party AI Coding Agents

T3 Code does not provide its own AI models. Code generation quality, response speed, and usage limits depend on the underlying Providers.

Before using it, make sure the corresponding tools have completed authentication, your account subscription or API credits are sufficient, and the CLI version is compatible with the current version of T3 Code.

If an agent fails to execute a request, check the Provider’s service status and authentication information first.

3. Automated Permissions Do Not Mean Zero Operational Risk

T3 Code provides different permission modes, but granting higher permissions allows agents to perform operations such as modifying files and executing terminal commands.

For high-risk tasks involving file deletion, configuration changes, or system commands, it is recommended to retain manual approval and review commands and modification scopes before execution.

V. FAQ

Q1: Which AI Coding Tools Does T3 Code Support?

T3 Code currently supports Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Grok Build, OpenCode, Antigravity, and other tools. Additional compatible agents can also be integrated through methods such as ACP. The actual supported tools depend on the current version.

Q2: Can T3 Code Run Multiple AI Agents Simultaneously?

Yes. Users can create multiple Threads to let different agents handle tasks in parallel. Git Worktrees can also be used to isolate coding environments. The actual number of parallel tasks depends on available device resources and Provider usage limits.

Q3: Does T3 Code Need to Run on a Computer All the Time?

If agents run in a local environment, the computer or server must remain powered on. Remote access only allows you to switch devices for managing tasks; it does not automatically move the tasks to the cloud.

VI. Conclusion

The main value of T3 Code lies in its ability to centrally manage multiple AI coding agents, simplify task assignment, and support parallel development. It is suitable for developers who need to switch between agents, manage multiple projects, and monitor tasks remotely.

However, its actual capabilities are still subject to third-party services and runtime environments. Before using it, make sure your accounts, permissions, and environment configurations are properly set up.

items.title: At a major Silicon Valley AI conference, VCs and CEOs grapple with a future without Jensen Huang
items.summary: Pranav Dixit/Business Insider Jensen Huang's exit dominated conversations at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit. Founders and investors worried about losing a powerful backer of AI startups. Some said Nvidia's chip lead would endure, while rivals saw an opening. Hours after he was ousted as the CEO of Nvidia, Jensen Huang was still winning at the Cerebral Valley AI Summit in San Francisco on Thursday. At least in a video game. In "Cerebral Combat," an arcade game set up for attendees, the Nvidia cofounder could take down Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg with a giant GPU. Outside the game, things weren't going nearly as well for Huang. Hours after his ouster as Nvidia's CEO, Jensen Huang was still winning — in a video game. Pranav Dixit/Business Insider On Thursday morning, he had resigned as CEO of Nvidia, the company he founded 33 years ago and built into the world's most valuable chipmaker, following reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman suspected by US intelligence officials of spying for China. Nvidia named its longtime CFO, Colette Kress , interim CEO. The news was hard to escape at the summit, where hundreds of founders, investors, and tech executives had gathered to talk about AI's future. One venture capitalist asked Business Insider's Katie Roof , who was wearing black, whether she was attending Huang's funeral. The jokes masked a genuine worry: What happens to the AI boom when one of its biggest financial backers is suddenly gone? Ali Ghodsi, CEO of Databricks, a data and AI software company backed by Nvidia, said onstage that Huang had become something of a safety net for AI startups. Whenever investors worried about a bubble, he said, Huang was there to reassure them that Nvidia would help keep the industry going. Without him, that reassurance might be harder to come by. "On the margin, I think that starts hurting a lot of startups," Ghodsi said. Nvidia's importance to the AI industry goes well beyond the chips that power much of it. Under Huang, the company became one of Silicon Valley's most influential investors, earning a reputation as the "central bank of AI" for its willingness to bankroll startups that, in many cases, also buy its chips. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Sean Gallup/Getty Images Just how deeply Nvidia is embedded in the industry became clear at the summit. Venture capital firm Bessemer Venture Partners and Newcomer, the publication that organized the conference, unveiled a list of the world's 100 most important private AI companies. Nvidia had invested in 42 of them, according to Bessemer partner Talia Goldberg. That kind of influence is hard to replace. Hemant Taneja, CEO of venture capital firm General Catalyst, compared Nvidia's importance to that of the big banks during the 2008 financial crisis. The implication was hard to miss: Nvidia had become too big to fail, and a messy leadership transition could have consequences far beyond the company. "This is not a normal company," he said onstage, "and we all need to make sure the continuity of leadership in AI for us as a nation and for the industry at large remains." Nikesh Arora, CEO of cybersecurity giant Palo Alto Networks, was less worried about Nvidia's technology than about losing Huang himself. He described the Nvidia founder as an unusually generous champion of the industry, lending his time and influence to everything from open-source AI to cybersecurity. "Is there short-term instability in the moment?" he said onstage. "Most likely, because there's a whole bunch of parts of the ecosystem which need to reexamine where their champions are." Guillermo Rauch, CEO of Vercel, a cloud platform for developers, also worried about the future of Nvidia's support for open-source AI. Under Huang, Nvidia had become a major champion of the movement. In September, Nvidia agreed to acquire Hugging Face, a popular platform for sharing open-source AI models, for nearly $13 billion. "An Nvidia without Jensen is going to be, I think, a challenging one," Rauch said onstage. Still, he hoped the company's extensive partnerships would help preserve Huang's vision. Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora Camille Cohen/Camille Cohen for Newcomer Media For founders who work closely with Nvidia, the uncertainty was more immediate. Zuzanna Stamirowska, CEO of Pathway, a startup developing AI models, told Business Insider that Nvidia had been an unusually attentive partner, with employees constantly looking for opportunities to collaborate. Whether the company could preserve that culture without Huang was another matter. "I'd say we don't know yet," she said. Hassaan Raza, CEO of Tavus, a startup building AI-powered video agents, worried that any stumble at Nvidia could set back America's broader AI ambitions. Even a disappointing earnings report under new leadership, he suggested, could send shock waves through the industry. "If Nvidia misses a quarter in the next year or something, oh my gosh, it's going to be a bloodbath," Raza told Business Insider. Aravind Srinivas, CEO of AI search startup Perplexity, which counts Nvidia among its largest investors, said he had met with Nvidia executives earlier Thursday and found business proceeding as usual. Huang, he said, had built a company with technological advantages that wouldn't disappear overnight. "Even now, the best GPUs for running inference is Nvidia, and the best GPUs for running training is Nvidia, and none of that stops," Srinivas said. "It's established for years in the future." Databricks' Ghodsi, too, expected Nvidia to remain strong for at least another two or three years, thanks to the long development cycles for its chips. What happens after that was a different question. For Nvidia's competitors, meanwhile, Huang's abrupt exit presented an opening. Robert Wachen, cofounder of Etched , a startup developing specialized AI chips to challenge Nvidia, praised Huang's contributions to the industry before conceding that his departure could be good news for rivals. "Now we see there's probably going to be a big opening, which we plan to capitalize on," Wachen said onstage. There was at least some agreement that more competition would be good for AI. General Catalyst's Taneja suggested the upheaval could push startups to explore alternatives from AMD and Google rather than relying so heavily on Nvidia. Raza said that he agreed with Taneja. But he wasn't exactly celebrating. "This is not the best way to do it," he said, "but we'll be forced to do it." Have a tip? items.title: Company Brain: Your AI Agents Will Act on Whatever Your Records Say
items.summary: Take one duplicate account record. In a pipeline report, it inflates a number that an analyst can catch in review; in front of a prospecting agent, it becomes two outreach sequences to the same buyer, one addressed to a contact who left last year. The company brain, a shared layer of company context for AI agents, is meant to head off errors like that, yet the layer stores only what the business puts into it. What vendors mean by a company brain Vendors give the idea different names and different scopes. WRITER unveiled its Enterprise Brain on 9 September 2026 and describes it as a “governed, universal context layer” that captures brand knowledge, decision logic and live business data for teams and AI agents. CMSWire reports that Enterprise Brain is in early access for select customers. Microsoft announced Microsoft IQ at its Build conference earlier this year as a context layer that grounds agents in public and enterprise information , assembled from Work IQ, Fabric IQ, Foundry IQ and Web IQ. Coverage of both launches leaves one question open. CMSWire’s report does not explain how Enterprise Brain checks the accuracy of live business data, and IT Brief’s report on Microsoft IQ gives no detail on how its grounding works or how accurate it is. The vendor supplies the plumbing and the customer supplies the facts, so the accuracy question sits with the buyer. Agents turn data errors into actions Gartner has put numbers on the CRM version of this risk. Its Hype Cycle for CRM Technologies, 2025 predicts that by the end of 2028, at least 40% of agentic AI projects for CRM will fail or struggle because customer data lacks quality and consistency. A separate Gartner release from February 2025 predicts that organizations will abandon 60% of AI projects unsupported by AI-ready data through 2026. In the survey behind that release, covering 1,203 data management leaders, 63% said their organizations either lack the right data management practices for AI or cannot tell whether they have them. A dashboard shows a wrong number to a person who can doubt it, while an agent reads the same record and acts on it, so the error can reach a customer before anyone sees it. The case involved a chatbot, but its logic applies to any agent acting in a company’s name. Customer records supply the brain’s facts Sales agents draw their facts about customers from the CRM. Salesforce’s Prospecting Agent researches accounts across CRM history, call recordings, past emails and third-party data sources, then ranks who to target. HubSpot’s data quality tools flag duplicate contacts and companies, formatting issues and gaps in enrichment coverage. Flagging a duplicate is the easy half. The hard half is entity resolution, the task of deciding which records describe the same company. In practice, a legal name, a trading name and a rep’s shorthand can sit in three separate records, and a subsidiary can sit under the wrong parent. Public company registers, such as Companies House in the United Kingdom or the Kamer van Koophandel in the Netherlands, hold legal names and registration numbers, and commercial providers aggregate them. Both surveys carry limits. Data vendors ran them, and each sells data software. Collibra’s poll has a margin of error of 6.4 percentage points. Modern Data found that respondents running agents in production are nearly four times as likely to have engineered a context layer on purpose, and it notes that a snapshot cannot say whether the layer enabled the agents or the agents prompted the layer. Name an owner and a tie-breaker source My take: treat the company brain as a data-ownership project that happens to require software. Start with the fields agents read most, such as company name, parent company, contact role and account owner, and assign one named person to each. Pick the reference source that wins when two records disagree, and set an age limit after which an agent flags a record instead of acting on it. Log every correction an agent makes, because only 10% of Modern Data’s respondents keep both an audit trail of AI inputs and outputs and a link from decisions back to data sources, and without those two records nobody can trace a wrong email to the field that caused it. The most useful question to put to any company brain vendor is which source wins when two records disagree. The answer shows how much of the brain the buyer still has to build.

items.title: Jensen Huang Resigns: What Interim CEO Colette Kress Inherits Before Nvidia’s Earnings
items.summary: Nvidia now has a chief executive other than Jensen Huang for the first time in 33 years, and the new one reports quarterly results on Tuesday. Huang resigned Thursday as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, four days after the board opened an independent investigation tied to reports that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress runs the company on an interim basis, and the financing commitments she has explained to investors since August will now draw the closest scrutiny. What the board announced Nvidia’s announcement names three changes. Kress, who has served as CFO since joining Nvidia in September 2013 and spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft, keeps her finance role while she serves as interim CEO. Harvey C. Jones, a director since 1993 and a former CEO of Synopsys, becomes the first Chair of the Board in the company’s history. The board has started a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates. The release gives no reason for Huang’s exit and does not mention the independent investigation the board announced on November 8. The board opened that investigation after reporting that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted Huang, and he told employees in a letter the same day that he had been unfaithful to his wife. On November 11, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive who reports directly to him, a report that Nvidia and Huang had not confirmed as of Thursday. The Wall Street Journal reported the same day that the board was preparing to remove him, and Nvidia’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission lists November 11 as the date the board accepted his resignation. A market already under strain Nvidia entered the week weakened by a November 5 sell-off in AI stocks that gave the S&P 500 its worst day since April 2025, according to AP. Nvidia closed Wednesday at $173.73, then fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove Huang. Yahoo Finance data showed the stock at $154.68 before Thursday’s open, about 11% below that close. Shares fell as much as 14% during the session, briefly erasing about $600 billion in market value, CNN reported, before closing down 4.3% at $166.19. NBC News reported that Nvidia’s market value dipped below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 in early trading and ended the day barely above that line, after losing about $500 billion this week. The recovery from the low suggests some investors treat the leadership change as a manageable event rather than a verdict on demand, and CNN reported heavy retail buying on Thursday morning. Analysts moved the other way. CNBC counted at least six downgrades between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, and Dan Ives of Yorkville valued Nvidia at $225 a share without Huang, against $300 with him. The financing commitments Kress inherits Kress takes over a company whose obligations are growing faster than its sales. Supply and capacity commitments more than doubled in the quarter ended July 26, from $119 billion to $279 billion, mostly for memory, according to Nvidia’s CFO commentary. In August, Nvidia also agreed to guarantees capped at $105 billion that back data center leases for OpenAI at an Ohio campus. Revenue for the same quarter rose 18% from the prior quarter to $96.2 billion, and Nvidia guided to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, for the current one. Kress has defended these arrangements in public. According to coverage of the August call, she acknowledged that critics call the support circular financing, and she said outside capital underwrites each deal and that Nvidia does not make loans. That history cuts both ways. She knows the commitments better than any outside candidate, and her continuity as CFO removes one execution risk from the handover. She also faces a test of credibility that a newly hired CEO would not: scaling back those commitments would reverse a strategy she has defended herself. A new chair and no named successor Until Thursday, Nvidia had no board chair. Its filings describe an independent lead director instead, a structure the board has said gives every member an equal voice. The board that created the Chair role must now run a CEO search while a congressional inquiry and Tuesday’s earnings call land within days. Semafor reported before the resignation that the board’s average tenure is nearly 15 years, about double the S&P 500 norm, and that three directors, Huang and Jones among them, have served since the 1993 founding. No successor stood ready. Bloomberg reported in January that Nvidia lacked a clear heir, and the board’s announcement names no candidate. Huang has said he has about 50 direct reports, and Semafor reported that Nvidia has no chief operating officer, a structure that leaves no executive in line to inherit the role by default. President Donald Trump supplied a name on Truth Social, writing that only Tim Cook, Apple’s executive chairman, could take Huang’s place, and adding, “A Legend replaces a Legend!”
items.summary_html:
Nvidia now has a chief executive other than Jensen Huang for the first time in 33 years, and the new one reports quarterly results on Tuesday. Huang resigned Thursday as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, four days after the board opened an independent investigation tied to reports that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him. Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress runs the company on an interim basis, and the financing commitments she has explained to investors since August will now draw the closest scrutiny.

What the board announced

Nvidia’s announcement names three changes. Kress, who has served as CFO since joining Nvidia in September 2013 and spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies including Cisco and Microsoft, keeps her finance role while she serves as interim CEO. Harvey C. Jones, a director since 1993 and a former CEO of Synopsys, becomes the first Chair of the Board in the company’s history. The board has started a search for a permanent CEO and will consider internal and external candidates.

The release gives no reason for Huang’s exit and does not mention the independent investigation the board announced on November 8. The board opened that investigation after reporting that a foreign intelligence effort had targeted Huang, and he told employees in a letter the same day that he had been unfaithful to his wife. On November 11, The New York Times reported a second relationship, with a senior Nvidia executive who reports directly to him, a report that Nvidia and Huang had not confirmed as of Thursday. The Wall Street Journal reported the same day that the board was preparing to remove him, and Nvidia’s filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission lists November 11 as the date the board accepted his resignation.

A market already under strain

Nvidia entered the week weakened by a November 5 sell-off in AI stocks that gave the S&P 500 its worst day since April 2025, according to AP. Nvidia closed Wednesday at $173.73, then fell more than 8% in after-hours trading after the Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to remove Huang. Yahoo Finance data showed the stock at $154.68 before Thursday’s open, about 11% below that close. Shares fell as much as 14% during the session, briefly erasing about $600 billion in market value, CNN reported, before closing down 4.3% at $166.19. NBC News reported that Nvidia’s market value dipped below $4 trillion for the first time since 2025 in early trading and ended the day barely above that line, after losing about $500 billion this week.

The recovery from the low suggests some investors treat the leadership change as a manageable event rather than a verdict on demand, and CNN reported heavy retail buying on Thursday morning. Analysts moved the other way. CNBC counted at least six downgrades between Wednesday night and Thursday morning, and Dan Ives of Yorkville valued Nvidia at $225 a share without Huang, against $300 with him.

The financing commitments Kress inherits

Kress takes over a company whose obligations are growing faster than its sales. Supply and capacity commitments more than doubled in the quarter ended July 26, from $119 billion to $279 billion, mostly for memory, according to Nvidia’s CFO commentary. In August, Nvidia also agreed to guarantees capped at $105 billion that back data center leases for OpenAI at an Ohio campus. Revenue for the same quarter rose 18% from the prior quarter to $96.2 billion, and Nvidia guided to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, for the current one.

Kress has defended these arrangements in public. According to coverage of the August call, she acknowledged that critics call the support circular financing, and she said outside capital underwrites each deal and that Nvidia does not make loans. That history cuts both ways. She knows the commitments better than any outside candidate, and her continuity as CFO removes one execution risk from the handover. She also faces a test of credibility that a newly hired CEO would not: scaling back those commitments would reverse a strategy she has defended herself.

A new chair and no named successor

Until Thursday, Nvidia had no board chair. Its filings describe an independent lead director instead, a structure the board has said gives every member an equal voice. The board that created the Chair role must now run a CEO search while a congressional inquiry and Tuesday’s earnings call land within days. Semafor reported before the resignation that the board’s average tenure is nearly 15 years, about double the S&P 500 norm, and that three directors, Huang and Jones among them, have served since the 1993 founding.

No successor stood ready. Bloomberg reported in January that Nvidia lacked a clear heir, and the board’s announcement names no candidate. Huang has said he has about 50 direct reports, and Semafor reported that Nvidia has no chief operating officer, a structure that leaves no executive in line to inherit the role by default. President Donald Trump supplied a name on Truth Social, writing that only Tim Cook, Apple’s executive chairman, could take Huang’s place, and adding, “A Legend replaces a Legend!” The post suggests the White House expects a voice in the choice of a successor, which will make an independent search harder to demonstrate.

Public backing did not change the outcome. Trump said on November 8 that Huang should remain CEO, and Elon Musk endorsed a post the next day calling Huang irreplaceable. On Wednesday evening, hours before the announcement, Musk answered a post from the financial blog ZeroHedge urging him to hire Huang with “That would be an honor,” though he named no role and no offer has been reported. After the resignation, Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao called it a mistake for Nvidia to let Huang go. The board alone chooses the next CEO, and Huang owned less than 4% of Nvidia, according to its proxy statement, with no super-voting stock.

Washington stays in the frame

Huang’s resignation does not end the congressional inquiry. He agreed Wednesday to testify before the US Congress by Thanksgiving, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Brian Mast said Thursday, after lawmakers threatened a subpoena. The session will run behind closed doors, and Mast expects it to be recorded and transcribed. Three Republican House chairs had asked for a briefing on Huang’s dealings with a former executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore company that buys Nvidia chips, and on Nvidia’s safeguards against foreign espionage.

Public evidence remains thin on the central question. Nvidia’s board said on November 8 that it had no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised. The Times reported that officials did not believe Huang knew the executive might be gathering information for China, and China’s foreign ministry has called the spy allegation unsubstantiated. No charges have been reported.

Export policy gives the story its commercial weight. Huang campaigned against tighter limits on chip sales to China, and the Trump administration approved H200 exports to China in December 2025 under conditions that include inspections and a 25% tariff, according to Al Jazeera. Nvidia’s guidance excludes any China data center compute revenue, so a reopening of that market would be upside, and a hearing about the former CEO’s contacts makes that upside harder to forecast.

What to watch on Tuesday

Nvidia reports at about 1:20 p.m. PT, with its call at 2 p.m. PT. Investors will look first for whether Kress reaffirms the $108 billion outlook and the commitments behind it. They will also listen for a timeline on the CEO search, since an interim arrangement without one invites speculation. A third signal is how management talks about China and export policy now that Huang, who lobbied Washington on those rules, no longer leads the company.

Jones said in the announcement that the board expects “operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” and Tuesday’s numbers will show whether demand agrees. The harder test comes later, when a permanent CEO must hold the financing commitments and the relationship with Washington together. A board that appointed its first chair only this week has to choose that person under political scrutiny.

items.title: Microsoft 365 Outage: Failing Server Health Checks Took Down Outlook, Teams and Copilot
items.summary: A large number of Microsoft’s own servers dropped out of service on Thursday, November 12, 2026, cutting off Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online and Copilot for users across the Americas and, by Friday morning, Australia. As of about 7:15 p.m. Eastern Time (ET), Microsoft had not declared the outage over and had not published a root cause. A company spokesperson told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) there was “no indication this is a cyber attack.” How the Outage Unfolded Trouble started in the morning, when Microsoft said it was investigating problems with Teams for users in North America. The company later said its mitigation had restored that service, and it has not said whether that incident is related to the larger one. The larger failure arrived in the early afternoon. Variety reported that user complaints about Outlook began spiking around 12:39 p.m. ET, and at 12:54 p.m. the Microsoft 365 Status account on X acknowledged that users were struggling to reach Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas. Microsoft tracked the mailbox problem as incident EX1550543 and opened a wider advisory, MO1550821, which BleepingComputer reported as starting at 1:26 p.m. ET. That advisory named Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender XDR. As the afternoon went on, the list grew. Forbes Australia’s tally added Planner, To Do, Intune, Defender for Office 365, Purview, Power BI and the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Microsoft also warned that the problem could affect connectivity for users in any region. Scale is hard to pin down. Downdetector counts user-submitted reports rather than affected accounts, and it recorded 138,058 Outlook reports around 1 p.m. ET, according to Reuters . Fox Business , citing Dynamics Connect, put Microsoft 365’s user base at roughly 321 million, though that is a third-party estimate. What Microsoft Says Went Wrong Microsoft’s explanation shifted as the day went on, which is normal in a live incident and worth reading closely. The first public diagnosis was elevated load on part of its infrastructure across multiple regions. Microsoft then refined that. The load, it said, was not coming from extra traffic but from “a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” which strained the machines still running. It said it had paused deployments, was moving traffic off the affected infrastructure and was restarting servers. Soon after, it tied the unavailable servers to failed automated health checks. In mid-afternoon Microsoft said it had found no recent change that lined up with the start of the impact, but that the failed health checks might come from a specific component that processes server health. It began deploying a change to bypass that component on a subset of servers and started looking into why the affected servers showed elevated processor usage. Around 4 p.m. ET, CNBC reported , Microsoft said an alternative health check method had let some servers return to service, and it began applying the method more broadly. Microsoft added two details over the following hours. It said a small number of configuration updates were under investigation as potential contributors and, by about 5 p.m. ET, that a core process on the affected servers was becoming overwhelmed. The first detail sits awkwardly beside the earlier statement that no recent change matched the start of the impact. The two can be reconciled, since a configuration update may contribute to a failure without lining up with its first minute, but Microsoft has not yet explained how those updates relate to the health check component. Progress was uneven. Microsoft said its actions so far had not provided the relief it expected . By about 6 p.m. ET it reported that a portion of the affected servers had returned to service and were holding stable, and it told users to expect a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect. Reuters reported that Outlook reports on Downdetector had fallen to about 34,490 by evening. A falling count is not the same as a working inbox: TechRadar’s live coverage noted at roughly the same hour that access had not returned for everyone, or even for most users. Then came a setback. By about 7:15 p.m. ET Microsoft reported, as ABC’s live coverage relayed , that servers it had brought back could become unresponsive again once they started taking traffic. It responded by limiting which types of traffic could reach the affected infrastructure in some locations, and by rebuilding a subset of servers on a previous software configuration to test whether that stops them becoming unresponsive. Why Recovery Was Slow This section is analysis, not a diagnosis Microsoft has confirmed. Microsoft’s updates describe a loop that is familiar in large server fleets. When health checks pull servers out of rotation, the remaining servers absorb their traffic, and each further loss raises the load on the survivors. Restarting machines helps only if they can withstand the traffic that returns to them, and that is exactly where Microsoft reported trouble. Mark Gregory, an associate professor at RMIT University in Australia, offered a similar reading to the ABC. Many servers appeared to have dropped off the list of available servers, he said, leaving the rest unable to carry all the traffic. If that reading is right, a restart is not a recovery. Engineers have to rebuild capacity gradually and throttle demand while they do it, which is consistent with Microsoft’s decision to restrict some traffic types. Who Felt the Outage In the US, the Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget said state government was having trouble with email and other Microsoft apps. Michigan Medicine reported problems reaching Outlook and other Microsoft applications, and sources told The Detroit News that Henry Ford Health lost access to Outlook and Teams. In Canada, CP24 reported that a Toronto hospital network declared a “Code Grey,” the designation for a loss or failure of infrastructure, and that Via Rail services were affected. In Australia, where the outage arrived on Friday morning, Service NSW reported that some transactions at its service and call centres were unavailable. According to the Australian Associated Press, NSW Parliament, the Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory governments, local councils and Queensland Health were also affected. A Home Affairs spokesperson said Australia’s National Cyber Security Coordinator, Lieutenant General Michelle McGuinness, was looking into the outage. Reuters reported at least one direct business consequence: the US electric truck maker Workhorse Group moved its third-quarter results announcement from November 12 to November 16, citing business disruption from the outage. Sign-in problems added a second layer of pain. ABC reported that some users said the Outlook failure also locked them out of other services because they could not use two-factor authentication codes to log in. AI Assistants Inherited the Outage Copilot sat on the advisory’s list of affected services, and the damage reached beyond Microsoft’s own assistant. Reuters reported that the outage also hit connectors used by OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI services. OpenAI said new connections to Microsoft connectors might be broken and that tools might not work as expected. Anthropic said an issue with an upstream provider was affecting its Microsoft 365 connector. The implication is that an AI assistant connected to a mailbox is only as available as the mailbox. When Exchange Online fails, an agent that drafts replies, summarizes threads or schedules meetings has nothing to read and nothing to act on, whichever company built the agent. Companies that have layered AI features on top of Microsoft 365 should count Microsoft’s availability in their AI risk assessment as well as their IT risk assessment. What the Outage Was Not Downdetector also showed spikes for Azure, but Microsoft’s advisory for the incident did not list Azure among the affected services. CNBC reported that Amazon Web Services said it was operating normally and flagged inaccurate outage reports on its platforms, while Tom’s Guide saw reports appear for Gmail, Zoom and Yahoo Mail. One plausible explanation, though not one the trackers confirm, is that people check other services when a dominant one fails, which inflates report counts elsewhere. On the question of an attack, Microsoft has said there is no indication of one. Its own description, a loss of server capacity under ordinary demand rather than an overload of traffic, is also not what a flood-style attack typically looks like. A Pattern in How Microsoft’s Outages Begin Thursday’s failure fits a run of incidents in which Microsoft’s own accounts point inward. On October 29, 2025, an Azure Front Door outage degraded Microsoft services and customer sites from 15:45 UTC until 00:05 UTC on October 30. Microsoft confirmed an inadvertent configuration change as the trigger. On January 22 and 23, 2026, The Register reported , Microsoft 365 was disrupted for nearly 10 hours, and Microsoft blamed part of its North American infrastructure for not processing traffic as expected. Tom’s Guide reported that Microsoft also cited elevated service load combined with temporary capacity constraints during maintenance. On July 23, 2026, according to BleepingComputer , a bug in the system that converts maintenance requests into machine-readable instructions wrongly tagged extra network devices, and routes were removed from more devices than intended in Microsoft’s West US region. Microsoft rolled the change back, and services were fully restored by 3:41 p.m. ET. On the Azure side, Microsoft’s status history records that from 20:30 UTC on September 30 to 02:15 UTC on October 1, several Azure networking services returned intermittent failures on management operations as a rolling update moved through the regions. The impact ended once Microsoft finished rolling back a change that had increased control plane processing time. In each of those four cases, Microsoft’s own account points to its internal change, maintenance or capacity handling rather than an outside attack. Thursday’s cause is unconfirmed, so adding it to the list would be premature. Microsoft’s references to a health check component and to configuration updates under investigation point in the same direction. What IT Leaders Should Take From It Keep an incident channel that does not run on the suite that is failing. During Thursday’s outage Microsoft pointed administrators to status.cloud.microsoft for details when the admin center was unavailable, and ABC10 reported that the status page itself had loading errors at one point. A team that coordinates its response in Teams and Outlook has no coordination at the moment it needs it most. Map which sign-ins depend on a mailbox, because lockouts compounded the damage for some users. Then ask each AI vendor in your stack which Microsoft connectors its agents rely on, and write down what the business does by hand when those connectors stop. items.summary_html:
A large number of Microsoft’s own servers dropped out of service on Thursday, November 12, 2026, cutting off Outlook, Teams, SharePoint Online and Copilot for users across the Americas and, by Friday morning, Australia. As of about 7:15 p.m. Eastern Time (ET), Microsoft had not declared the outage over and had not published a root cause. A company spokesperson told the Australian Broadcasting Corporation (ABC) there was “no indication this is a cyber attack.”

How the Outage Unfolded

Trouble started in the morning, when Microsoft said it was investigating problems with Teams for users in North America. The company later said its mitigation had restored that service, and it has not said whether that incident is related to the larger one. The larger failure arrived in the early afternoon. Variety reported that user complaints about Outlook began spiking around 12:39 p.m. ET, and at 12:54 p.m. the Microsoft 365 Status account on X acknowledged that users were struggling to reach Exchange Online mailboxes in the Americas.

Microsoft tracked the mailbox problem as incident EX1550543 and opened a wider advisory, MO1550821, which BleepingComputer reported as starting at 1:26 p.m. ET. That advisory named Exchange Online, Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Defender XDR. As the afternoon went on, the list grew. Forbes Australia’s tally added Planner, To Do, Intune, Defender for Office 365, Purview, Power BI and the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center. Microsoft also warned that the problem could affect connectivity for users in any region.

Scale is hard to pin down. Downdetector counts user-submitted reports rather than affected accounts, and it recorded 138,058 Outlook reports around 1 p.m. ET, according to Reuters. Fox Business, citing Dynamics Connect, put Microsoft 365’s user base at roughly 321 million, though that is a third-party estimate.

What Microsoft Says Went Wrong

Microsoft’s explanation shifted as the day went on, which is normal in a live incident and worth reading closely. The first public diagnosis was elevated load on part of its infrastructure across multiple regions. Microsoft then refined that. The load, it said, was not coming from extra traffic but from “a number of servers being unexpectedly unavailable,” which strained the machines still running. It said it had paused deployments, was moving traffic off the affected infrastructure and was restarting servers. Soon after, it tied the unavailable servers to failed automated health checks.

In mid-afternoon Microsoft said it had found no recent change that lined up with the start of the impact, but that the failed health checks might come from a specific component that processes server health. It began deploying a change to bypass that component on a subset of servers and started looking into why the affected servers showed elevated processor usage. Around 4 p.m. ET, CNBC reported, Microsoft said an alternative health check method had let some servers return to service, and it began applying the method more broadly.

Microsoft added two details over the following hours. It said a small number of configuration updates were under investigation as potential contributors and, by about 5 p.m. ET, that a core process on the affected servers was becoming overwhelmed. The first detail sits awkwardly beside the earlier statement that no recent change matched the start of the impact. The two can be reconciled, since a configuration update may contribute to a failure without lining up with its first minute, but Microsoft has not yet explained how those updates relate to the health check component.

Progress was uneven. Microsoft said its actions so far had not provided the relief it expected. By about 6 p.m. ET it reported that a portion of the affected servers had returned to service and were holding stable, and it told users to expect a gradual recovery as their clients reconnect. Reuters reported that Outlook reports on Downdetector had fallen to about 34,490 by evening. A falling count is not the same as a working inbox: TechRadar’s live coverage noted at roughly the same hour that access had not returned for everyone, or even for most users.

Then came a setback. By about 7:15 p.m. ET Microsoft reported, as ABC’s live coverage relayed, that servers it had brought back could become unresponsive again once they started taking traffic. It responded by limiting which types of traffic could reach the affected infrastructure in some locations, and by rebuilding a subset of servers on a previous software configuration to test whether that stops them becoming unresponsive.

Why Recovery Was Slow

This section is analysis, not a diagnosis Microsoft has confirmed. Microsoft’s updates describe a loop that is familiar in large server fleets. When health checks pull servers out of rotation, the remaining servers absorb their traffic, and each further loss raises the load on the survivors. Restarting machines helps only if they can withstand the traffic that returns to them, and that is exactly where Microsoft reported trouble.

Mark Gregory, an associate professor at RMIT University in Australia, offered a similar reading to the ABC. Many servers appeared to have dropped off the list of available servers, he said, leaving the rest unable to carry all the traffic. If that reading is right, a restart is not a recovery. Engineers have to rebuild capacity gradually and throttle demand while they do it, which is consistent with Microsoft’s decision to restrict some traffic types.

Who Felt the Outage

In the US, the Michigan Department of Technology, Management & Budget said state government was having trouble with email and other Microsoft apps. Michigan Medicine reported problems reaching Outlook and other Microsoft applications, and sources told The Detroit News that Henry Ford Health lost access to Outlook and Teams. In Canada, CP24 reported that a Toronto hospital network declared a “Code Grey,” the designation for a loss or failure of infrastructure, and that Via Rail services were affected.

In Australia, where the outage arrived on Friday morning, Service NSW reported that some transactions at its service and call centres were unavailable. According to the Australian Associated Press, NSW Parliament, the Australian Capital Territory and Northern Territory governments, local councils and Queensland Health were also affected. A Home Affairs spokesperson said Australia’s National Cyber Security Coordinator, Lieutenant General Michelle McGuinness, was looking into the outage.

Reuters reported at least one direct business consequence: the US electric truck maker Workhorse Group moved its third-quarter results announcement from November 12 to November 16, citing business disruption from the outage. Sign-in problems added a second layer of pain. ABC reported that some users said the Outlook failure also locked them out of other services because they could not use two-factor authentication codes to log in.

AI Assistants Inherited the Outage

Copilot sat on the advisory’s list of affected services, and the damage reached beyond Microsoft’s own assistant. Reuters reported that the outage also hit connectors used by OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s AI services. OpenAI said new connections to Microsoft connectors might be broken and that tools might not work as expected. Anthropic said an issue with an upstream provider was affecting its Microsoft 365 connector.

The implication is that an AI assistant connected to a mailbox is only as available as the mailbox. When Exchange Online fails, an agent that drafts replies, summarizes threads or schedules meetings has nothing to read and nothing to act on, whichever company built the agent. Companies that have layered AI features on top of Microsoft 365 should count Microsoft’s availability in their AI risk assessment as well as their IT risk assessment.

What the Outage Was Not

Downdetector also showed spikes for Azure, but Microsoft’s advisory for the incident did not list Azure among the affected services. CNBC reported that Amazon Web Services said it was operating normally and flagged inaccurate outage reports on its platforms, while Tom’s Guide saw reports appear for Gmail, Zoom and Yahoo Mail. One plausible explanation, though not one the trackers confirm, is that people check other services when a dominant one fails, which inflates report counts elsewhere.

On the question of an attack, Microsoft has said there is no indication of one. Its own description, a loss of server capacity under ordinary demand rather than an overload of traffic, is also not what a flood-style attack typically looks like.

A Pattern in How Microsoft’s Outages Begin

Thursday’s failure fits a run of incidents in which Microsoft’s own accounts point inward. On October 29, 2025, an Azure Front Door outage degraded Microsoft services and customer sites from 15:45 UTC until 00:05 UTC on October 30. Microsoft confirmed an inadvertent configuration change as the trigger. On January 22 and 23, 2026, The Register reported, Microsoft 365 was disrupted for nearly 10 hours, and Microsoft blamed part of its North American infrastructure for not processing traffic as expected. Tom’s Guide reported that Microsoft also cited elevated service load combined with temporary capacity constraints during maintenance.

On July 23, 2026, according to BleepingComputer, a bug in the system that converts maintenance requests into machine-readable instructions wrongly tagged extra network devices, and routes were removed from more devices than intended in Microsoft’s West US region. Microsoft rolled the change back, and services were fully restored by 3:41 p.m. ET. On the Azure side, Microsoft’s status history records that from 20:30 UTC on September 30 to 02:15 UTC on October 1, several Azure networking services returned intermittent failures on management operations as a rolling update moved through the regions. The impact ended once Microsoft finished rolling back a change that had increased control plane processing time.

In each of those four cases, Microsoft’s own account points to its internal change, maintenance or capacity handling rather than an outside attack. Thursday’s cause is unconfirmed, so adding it to the list would be premature. Microsoft’s references to a health check component and to configuration updates under investigation point in the same direction.

What IT Leaders Should Take From It

Keep an incident channel that does not run on the suite that is failing. During Thursday’s outage Microsoft pointed administrators to status.cloud.microsoft for details when the admin center was unavailable, and ABC10 reported that the status page itself had loading errors at one point. A team that coordinates its response in Teams and Outlook has no coordination at the moment it needs it most.

Map which sign-ins depend on a mailbox, because lockouts compounded the damage for some users. Then ask each AI vendor in your stack which Microsoft connectors its agents rely on, and write down what the business does by hand when those connectors stop.

What to Watch Next

As of Thursday evening, Microsoft had not published a post-incident review for the outage. When one arrives, three answers will matter most: why servers failed their health checks, why restored servers froze again under traffic, and what the configuration updates under investigation actually changed. After the July incident Microsoft said it would review its safety checks and its maintenance automation, so the test this time is whether the review names a cause specific enough to prevent a repeat.

items.title: Abrupt End to Nvidia’s Jensen Drama Leaves Unanswered Questions
items.summary: Jensen Huang’s long-running Nvidia drama ended on a cliffhanger with the news of the CEO’s resignation Thursday morning. We’re going to have to wait a while for the scriptwriters to figure out the next installment of this thriller. At the moment, we’ve got far more questions than answers: What happened between Sunday, when the board said it had confidence in Huang, and Wednesday night when Huang quit (as Nvidia revealed in a securities filing today)? What role did the Trump administration play in his departure? Astute watchers of the news media might have noticed that many of the numerous stories about the Wednesday night board meeting called to consider Huang’s future were at least partly written by Washington correspondents not normally reporting on Nvidia’s doings. Was the White House leaking stuff to pressure Huang to go? The answers will eventually come out, to be sure.

items.title: Inside Jensen Huang's Final Hours as the CEO of Nvidia
items.summary: At the end, Jensen Huang looked broken and shattered, his legendary energy depleted. After weeks spent denying the allegations of infidelity and fighting to remain in his job as Nvidia Corp.’s chief executive officer, his surrender late Wednesday night was unconditional. Huang’s usual take-charge demeanor had evaporated, according to a person familiar with the situation, and he’d started using phrases like “whatever” and “I don’t care.”
